note: Birnbaum et al. reported 13 patients with the Ashkenazi Jewish founder variant and Turkyilmaz et al. described 2 siblings with a novel variant, making the founder variant ~87% of published cases.

evidence.text: Thirteen patients from eight Ashkenazi Jewish families were identified carrying the identical homozygous frameshift founder variant in SGSM3.

source.quote: We identified 13 patients from 8 families of Ashkenazi Jewish origin who all carried the same homozygous frameshift variant in SGSM3 gene.

evidence.text: A homozygous stop-gain variant in SGSM3 was identified in two siblings, representing the only other published cohort of bi-allelic SGSM3-related intellectual disability.

source.title: A Strong Candidate Gene for Nonsyndromic Intellectual Disability Phenotype: SGSM3
source.quote: In this study, a novel homozygous stop-gain (NM_015705.6: c.1576C>T: p.(Arg526Ter)) variation was detected in the SGSM3 gene in two siblings with short stature and ID findings.

numbers.metric: siblings identified with non-founder SGSM3 variant
